definition: A model that makes predictions by learning a hierarchy of if-then splitting rules based on input features, forming a tree structure.
details: Decision trees are interpretable and easy to visualize, but individual trees can overfit; they're often combined into ensembles (like random forests or gradient boosting) for better performance.
story: Think of a lightbulb moment: the idea was always there, but someone had to point a finger at it. Boil it down and it is this: A model that makes predictions by learning a hierarchy of if-then splitting rules based on input features, forming a tree structure. Here is why it matters: Decision trees are interpretable and easy to visualize, but individual trees can overfit; they're often combined into ensembles (like random forests or gradient boosting) for better performance. Once you see it, you cannot unsee it. And that idea, made concrete, is Decision Tree.
